resources.string: Share your connection with the devices around you.
You\'re not sharing anything right now.
For the ShareNet app on another phone (client mode)
1. On the other device, open Wi-Fi settings and join the network below. Enter the password when it asks.
2. Then open that device\'s proxy settings and use the address below. On Android, that\'s under Wi-Fi → the network → Modify → Advanced → Proxy. On a computer, it\'s in the network\'s settings.
One honest note: a few apps ignore proxy settings, and most games and video calls need extra support. The client mode below adds that for Android.
1. First join the host\'s network in your Wi-Fi settings — they\'ll share the name and password.
2. Then enter the host\'s address below (usually 192.168.49.1) and the pairing PIN the host shows on its screen. Android will ask you to allow the connection — that\'s expected.
3. Games, calls, and streaming now work through the host. For browsing, also set the proxy as described above.
Android didn\'t allow the connection. Try again and accept the prompt.
The connection to the host was lost. Check that the host is still sharing, then reconnect.
The host rejected the pairing PIN. Check the PIN shown on the host\'s screen and try again.
Your phone may have a built-in shortcut

If this phone runs Android 13 or newer, try this first: connect to Wi-Fi, then switch on your hotspot in Settings. Many phones share the Wi-Fi connection with no extra battery cost. Not every phone can do it — and ShareNet works on all of them either way.
We need permission to find nearby devices and show notifications before sharing.
The hotspot couldn\'t start. Try turning Wi-Fi off and on, then start again.
The hotspot was closed by the system.
The connection couldn\'t be set up on this phone.
